scores.claim_text: Rollup thesis: space-infrastructure rollup (Made In Space, Adcole, Roccor, Hera) extended by $1.024B Edge Autonomy (UAS) acquisition in 2025.

supports.result: Multiple 8-Ks confirm Edge Autonomy deal (Jan 2025 announcement, June 2025 close); each prior acquisition individually documented in SEC filings. Mode A passes — each acquisition is real.

MIXED_COHERENCE: mean_coherence 0.74 across 5 acquisitions. Made In Space 0.95, Adcole 0.95, Roccor 0.85, Hera 0.80 — all high-coherence with the space-infrastructure thesis. EDGE AUTONOMY coherence 0.15 (low_coherence, is_revenue_synthetic=TRUE), $1.024B deal value. LLM reasoning: 'Edge Autonomy operates ground-based small unmanned aerial systems for terrestrial/EU defense customers; Redwire's thesis is in-space hardware and satellite platform integration. UAS and space-segment infrastructure are distinct technology verticals with no stated integration path or shared stack.'

Edge Autonomy added $107.1M FY25 revenue (32% of consolidated revenue per ICFR exclusion note) and $721M goodwill — i.e. dollar-for-dollar 'revenue synthesis' through a deal whose technology stack does not extend the space-segment thesis.

scores.M_value: Edge Autonomy rollup coherence 0.15 (revenue-synthetic) within an otherwise mixed ~0.73 mean. ICFR adjustment carves out 10% of assets and 32% of revenues from internal-controls assessment — the same Edge Autonomy bucket that the coherence model flags as off-thesis.
scores.interpretation: Even though each of Hera/MIS/Adcole/Roccor individually scores >=0.80, the $1.024B Edge Autonomy bolt-on is a classic Mode B finding: parent thesis is in-space hardware, but the largest acquisition is ground-launched small UAS for EU MoD customers. Per the framework heuristic, roll-up incoherence on the AGGREGATE is a distinct SEVE-class signal even when each acquisition is real, especially when the deal supplies the bulk of FY25 revenue growth (revenue-synthetic). Coupling with the material-weakness ICFR exclusion specifically for the Edge bucket amplifies the signal.

scores.claim_text: ICFR concluded NOT effective at Dec 31 2025; KPMG issued adverse opinion. Prior Lemen securities class action alleged material weaknesses; $8.0M settlement.

supports.result: REAFFIRMED_IN_STRUCTURED_DISCLOSURE: 2 subsequent filings within window (8-K 2026-05-06 and 10-Q 2026-05-07) both AFFIRMED the material-weakness disclosure; LLM-classified as ongoing, not remediated. ICFR weakness persists post-10K.
1 mention in DEF 14A (clawback boilerplate, classified UNRELATED). No financial-statement restatement triggered (yet).

KPMG issued an adverse opinion on ICFR for FY25. Material weaknesses cover (i) inability to fully deploy process-level controls across substantially all US operations; (ii) lack of ITGCs (program change and access controls) in European/remaining US ops. Edge Autonomy excluded from assessment though it represents 10% of assets and 32% of revenue.

Lemen securities class action (alleging material weaknesses in financial reporting) settled for $8.0M cash in 2025; derivative Yingling case settled with corporate governance reforms + $0.9M fees in Aug 2025.

scores.M_value: Adverse ICFR FY25 + REAFFIRMED material weakness in Q1 2026 10-Q + prior $8M Lemen settlement on the SAME material-weakness theme. Recurring pattern.
scores.interpretation: This is a textbook RED per the framework rubric: (a) ADVERSE ICFR opinion from auditor (KPMG), (b) recurring material-weakness pattern with prior securities litigation alleging the same, (c) reaffirmed in the very next 10-Q (the company has not remediated post-10K). Per heuristic 'Adverse ICFR or recurring material weakness is RED'.

scores.claim_text: $411.2M backlog ($299.8M Space + $111.4M Defense Tech) via direct federal and prime-contractor relationships.

supports.result: 117 federal awards totaling $238.6M, dominated by NASA (18 awards, biggest individual at $2.66M Industrial Crystallization Facility, $2.58M Biofabrication Facility, $2.50M INSPA Phase 2). DoD presence is real but small-dollar STTR/SBIR. Total $238.6M of historical federal obligations vs $411.2M backlog claim — backlog includes ESA / commercial / international (Ukraine/EU MoD via Edge) that USAspending wouldn't capture. Direct federal obligations don't bridge to backlog dollar value.

0 hits in Lockheed Martin's filings for 'Redwire'. Per heuristic 7, this is not penalized as SEVE because (a) Redwire is sub-tier (b) any single subcontractor relationship would be immaterial to LMT (c) Redwire's disclosure does not name LMT as a material counterparty — only generally references 'large prime contractors'.

scores.M_value: Federal obligations ($238.6M life-to-date) materially below disclosed $411.2M backlog. Lockheed zero-mention of Redwire is consistent with sub-tier disclosure threshold but does flag that the prime-contractor channel narrative is not corroborated at the named-prime level.
scores.interpretation: MODERATE: backlog claim plausibly bridges to international/ESA/commercial sources not in USAspending, but the gap is meaningful and the prime-contractor name-check fails at the Lockheed counterparty. Not RED (no specific named prime in the disclosure to contradict) but the federal obligations / backlog mismatch is a real Mode B underdelivery signal.

scores.claim_text: Stalker UAS granted DIU Authority to Operate / Blue UAS List on 2025-07-14; Penguin C heritage with Ukraine/Latvia/Lithuania/RSAF.

supports.result: 1 DoD award visible — N0001925P1000 to EDGE AUTONOMY SLO, LLC for $2.96M procuring 'VXE30 STALKER UAV ... in support of the Guyana Defence Force, Foreign Military Sales (FMS) case GU-P-LAG'. Confirms Stalker is a real, DoD-procured platform but the largest US contract is an FMS pass-through to Guyana, not a US-services Blue UAS deployment.

Only $3M visible US-DoD spend post-acquisition. Blue UAS listing should have produced a step-up in US-services orders if narrative is operative; visible obligations are minimal as of cutoff. Note that DIU/Blue UAS adoption is recent (Jul 2025) so timing-lag is plausible.

scores.M_value: Stalker is a real DoD-purchased platform (one $2.96M FMS award visible); the broader Blue UAS / U.S.-services adoption claim has not yet produced obligated revenue in USAspending. Foreign customers (Ukraine/Latvia/Lithuania/RSAF) are outside US registries by definition.
scores.interpretation: Stalker DIU Authority-to-Operate and Blue UAS listing are operative claims, but only one modest FMS award visible at the cutoff. Per heuristic 3 (planned vs operational) and the recent timing of the AtO, MODERATE rather than RED. Watch for new Edge / Redwire Defense Tech US-DoD awards in next two quarters.
